protocol.description:
Lets a desktop shell (a dock, a taskbar, a workspace overview) act on windows it doesn't own. It adds only the actions that no standard protocol offers, and works on the objects of standard protocols: toplevels are ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 objects from ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1, and workspaces are ext_workspace_handle_v1 objects from ext-workspace-v1. The results of a request are observed through those protocols (for example a workspace's active state), not through this one.
This global is privileged: the compositor only advertises it to clients it trusts, as it does ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1 and ext-workspace-v1.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: orbit_toplevel_manager_v1
interface.description: Requests take effect immediately, in the order they are sent; there is no commit. A request naming a toplevel that has been closed, or a workspace that has been removed, is ignored: either can happen at any time, so this is not a protocol error.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the manager. Requests already sent are not undone.

request.name: activate

description.summary: bring a toplevel to the user's attention and focus it

request.description:
Shows the workspace the toplevel is on (on its own output only; other outputs keep the workspace they show), restores it if it is minimized, raises it and gives it keyboard focus on the seat.
The compositor may keep keyboard focus elsewhere when something has to keep it, for example a lock screen or a launcher holding the keyboard exclusively; the toplevel then gets it once that ends.

request.name: move_to_workspace

description.summary: move a toplevel to a workspace

request.description: Moves the toplevel to the workspace, which may be on another output. No output changes the workspace it shows: the toplevel disappears from view if the workspace isn't shown, and appears if it is.

request.name: close
request.description: Asks the toplevel's client to close it, as the close button of a title bar does. The client decides: it may ask for confirmation first, or not close at all.

request.name: set_minimized
request.description: Hides the toplevel until it is unminimized or activated. Keyboard focus moves on as if the user had minimized it.

request.name: unset_minimized
request.description: Shows a minimized toplevel again where it was. It doesn't necessarily get keyboard focus; use activate for that. Ignored if the toplevel isn't minimized.

request.name: set_maximized
request.description: Maximizes the toplevel on its output.

request.name: unset_maximized
request.description: Returns a maximized toplevel to where it was before. Ignored if it isn't maximized.

request.name: get_state
request.description: Creates an object that reports the toplevel's state (focused, minimized, maximized, fullscreen). If the toplevel has already closed, the object never sends anything.

interface.name: orbit_toplevel_state_v1
interface.description: Reports the state of one toplevel. The first state event is sent right after the object is created, and another one each time the state changes. Once the toplevel closes, no more events are sent; the object stays valid until it is destroyed.

entry.name: activated
entry.summary: it has keyboard focus (at most one toplevel at a time)

event.name: state
event.description: The complete current state: an array of 32-bit unsigned values of the state enum, each at most once, in no particular order. An empty array means none of them.
